attempted_route: After re-inspecting production main and the live Savills workflows, ran a distinct indexed-domain recovery route: exact-date searches against catalogue.auctions.savills.co.uk, PropertyAuctions/PropertyAuctions.io, and general indexed web results for Savills 20 September 2012 plus year/date variants. This route independently surfaced contemporary indexed evidence for a Savills auction on 20 September 2012 (including the widely indexed Pink Floyd archive sale), but did not expose a surviving first-party catalogue URL, a PropertyAuctions AID/Auc LotList manifest, or a defensible commercial/mixed lot denominator. The evidence is therefore retained as an auction-date anchor only; no residential example is promoted into commercial history.
blocker: The 20 September 2012 auction date remains defensible, but the indexed-domain route still yields no source manifest that can enumerate its lots or classify a commercial/mixed subset. Without a surviving Savills catalogue/lot URL or PropertyAuctions AID/Auc manifest, canonical lot matches and unresolved commercial/mixed counts are intentionally null rather than inferred.
next_distinct_route: Move off search-engine indexing and enumerate archived URL inventories directly: Wayback CDX/Common Crawl prefix discovery for catalogue.auctions.savills.co.uk and historical Savills catalogue asset paths around 2012-09-20, then probe date-bearing archived catalogue/PDF/RSS assets. Separately enumerate PropertyAuctions AID ranges adjacent to verified 2011 and 2013 Savills events and accept only manifests whose embedded auctioneer/date fields identify Savills 2012; do not infer identity from numeric adjacency.

live_lot_expansion_run.note: This newer first-party lot-expansion run targets the 140-event live Savills archive index (2014 onward) and does not by itself resolve the 2012 manifest gap.
